question: What contamination reduction would count as practically meaningful for point-in-time legal QA, and thus what effect size must the design be powered to detect?
description: Power is only interpretable relative to an effect size considered worth detecting, and no retrieved work states how large a version-contamination reduction would count as practically important for legal QA. If the minimal interesting difference is large (for example 15 percentage points) while attainable strata are modest, even a feasible corpus yields an underpowered study; if it is small, the design may be adequate.
rationale: The census's go/no-go threshold needs a target effect size; the closest quantitative precedent is a point-in-time financial system reducing temporal leakage by roughly nine percentage points (10.8% to 1.7%), which can anchor the minimal interesting difference.
